lines.text: One fallen arch, and a channel choked with twenty years of mud. That was all that stood between the Lowmarket and clean water. Or so I thought.
On the second day, the kiln foreman came to see what the digging was about. Hobb had soot in every line of his face, and a low opinion of lords.
A royal ward, digging in our mud. A boy with no rings and no money. They'll call it charity.
I don't have any money. I have a plan, and a book on King Aldric's waterworks. Do you have bricks?
Ten thousand of them. And nobody to sell them to.
So the Lowmarket built it, hand to hand, brick by brick. Oswin shouted at them. They shouted back. He loved it.
Captain Holt had been sent to guard me. He had been carrying stones since the first afternoon. By the third week, he was arguing with Hobb about mortar.
On the twentieth day the arch stood whole, and we opened the sluice. The Lowmarket cheered.
Then it went into the hill under the city. And it never came out.
Twenty years, and still dry. Told you, my lord. The water hates us.
Water doesn't hate anybody. It just runs downhill. So we went down after it.
Under the streets ran tunnels older than the streets. Over one arch, someone had carved a king in a crown, with no rings behind his head.
I had seen that once before, on a queen in the Deep. I should have thought about it more.
A mile in, we found where our water went. Someone had bricked up the old channel, and cut a new one. Down, into the dark.
Seven rings around an eye, on every brick. The Order built this wall, my lord. That arch never stopped the water. It just gave everyone a reason not to look.
I didn't touch their wall. I went around it. Hobb's men cut a new channel in four nights, and nobody heard.
On the fifth morning, the fountains of the Lowmarket ran for the first time in twenty years.
It's cold. Gods, it's clean. Twenty years, zero. Two buckets at a time.
Twenty years! I'm going to wash my face. My wife won't know me.
That night in the kiln yard, I didn't say it aloud. Ilse had forbidden that. But the water was mine to keep running now. And so were they.
One by one, I felt them say yes. Sixty-three threads, thin and cold, smelling of smoke. My first in the city.
Tamsin wasn't at the fire. She had gone back down to the wall.
Downhill, my lord. Under the cathedral. Whatever the Order keeps down there, it has needed a lot of cold water. For twenty years.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter eighty-four, coming soon.
